mainEntity.name: What is the difference between meeting notes and minutes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The deciding difference is the approval vote. Notes never need one, while minutes only become official once the group adopts them. Under Robert's Rules (RONR, 12th edition), corrections raised at that vote go straight into the text, and the minutes are recorded as approved "as corrected" without listing the change.

No, and once approved they are much harder to change than notes. Robert's Rules (12th edition) requires a motion to Amend Something Previously Adopted to fix approved minutes. Even then, the secretary leaves the original wording alone and adds a margin note pointing to the correction. Your own notes carry no such rule.

Because a "minute" is also a brief note or memorandum. Merriam-Webster still lists that sense, with the example of someone sending the president "a minute explaining the problem". The plural took on a narrower job: the official record of a meeting's proceedings. The 1/60-of-an-hour meaning shares the word but not the purpose.

Usually a secretary, clerk or designated note-taker. In boards and associations the secretary drafts and signs them, but the members approve them, often by unanimous consent at the next meeting. Not the chair alone. Keep the 2 roles apart, since running a discussion and recording it at once usually means both suffer.

mainEntity.name: Should minutes include who said what?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Robert's Rules (RONR 12th ed., 48:2) calls summarizing debate in minutes improper, not just unnecessary. Name the member who made each main motion. The seconder's name, as Wikipedia's summary of minute-taking practice notes, is not strictly necessary. Quote someone directly only when the exact words could matter in a later dispute.

mainEntity.name: How soon should minutes be sent after a meeting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Send draft minutes within 1 to 2 business days, marked as a draft, then approve them at the next meeting. Some laws set an outer limit.
